On the stage, kyogen had begun.

The piece was <ruby>The No-Offering Sutra<rt>Fusenai-kyou</rt></ruby>. A priest finishes the memorial service, but the patron does not hand over the customary donation, and the priest is left standing there in total confusion. Honestly speaking, the sight was very funny.

Coming right after the long afterglow in my chest, this light exchange went in like a cup of tea after a meal and settled my <ruby>excitement<rt>excitement</rt></ruby>. A Noh program is thought out with great care, I told myself, and I admired it sincerely.

童心"Even now I see it in dreams. The impregnable fortress of Port ArthurRyuishun."
童心"In terrible cold, every time the buglebugle sent the soldiers charging... the whole frozen earth boiled with blood and flesh."
童心"Only allied corpses piling up... not one fragment of success in our hands, and those cursed walls not even scratched."
童心"Even the dragoon bombing had no effect. They were shot down, and ended by scattering their ammunition on our own men below."
童心"...It was hell, no. The three of us stood and watched that hell."
童心"I wept. Unworthy conduct for a warrior, I know, but the frailty of life and the cruelty of war went into my chest, and the tears would not stop..."
童心"Juutarou— our lord, you understand; that is what we called him in those days. Juutarou hit me. If I am crying for soldiers' deaths, he said, better I become a monk."
童心"Lord Yoritsuna said nothing. He just watched."
童心"That Hill 203. The hill where soldiers charged and charged again and piled up one more layer of bodies each time, he only watched it."
童心"He bit his lip hard... until blood showed. He must have bitten right through it..."
Sakurako"..."
童心"But afterwards. When we returned to headquarters, what did Lord Yoritsuna submit as his proposal? Lady Sakurako, can you guess?"
Sakurako"No..."

童心"But that sincerity moved General Nogi. The bombardment was carried out, and our forces finally seized Hill 203. The tide of the war turned in a single night."
童心"...Lord Yoritsuna truly knew how human lives may be usedused. What it really means to give a life a purpose!"
Sakurako"..."
童心"Did Lord Yoritsuna never tell the Princess such stories?"

Sakurako"...No. He very rarely spoke of war. When I was small, I sometimes begged him."
童心"Naturally. Naturally. The credit for the fall of that fortress was beyond doubt Lord Yoritsuna's, yet he never boasted of it, not even once."
童心"Rather, he held it his lifelong shame. That he had urged a general to fire on his own side."
童心"He did not regret it. But he was ashamed."
童心"That kind of man he was. Your father..."
Sakurako"...Father..."
童心"I tell you, Lady Sakurako, I do not want the many deeds of that Lord Yoritsuna to be buried."
童心"I want to leave his life correctly recorded for later generations. Having lived in the same age as him, I feel this responsibility is mine."
Sakurako"..."
童心"Will you permit it, Lady Sakurako? That we speak of Lord Yoritsuna?"
Sakurako"...Y..."
Sakurako"Yes..."

Princess Sakurako asked the question.

Her voice was <ruby>stiff and frozen<rt>・・・・</rt></ruby>, like laundry left hanging under a winter sky.

In the one-tenth of my mind that remained after ninety percent had gone blank, I thought: how ugly. The Princess's face, forcing itself to hold up a smile that was already collapsing, looked unbearably foul and ugly.

Can a human face become so ugly?

And across from her, how beautiful the monk looked.

Infinite joy. Love for everything in this world, with no edge and no bottom. It filled him to the brim: a smile that belonged to heaven.

It was as if the Buddha himself had descended.
